question.text: Under Rule 9(12) of the PML Rules, ongoing due diligence by a reporting entity includes which of the following activities?

answer.text: Close examination of transactions for consistency and source of funds where necessary, review of due-diligence measures when there are suspicions or doubts about prior identification data, and applying CDD to existing clients on the basis of materiality and risk
Only reviewing CDD records at the time of account opening and annual renewal
Applying enhanced due diligence to all existing customers uniformly, regardless of risk profile
Periodically reviewing CDD records and filing Suspicious Transaction Reports for all high-value transactions

explanation.text: The Logic: Rule 9(12) requires the reporting entity to (i) closely examine the transactions to ensure they are consistent with its knowledge of the client and risk profile, including source of funds where necessary, (ii) review the due-diligence measures where there are suspicions or doubts about the veracity or adequacy of previously obtained identification data, and (iii) apply CDD measures to existing clients on the basis of materiality and risk. The Trap: Ongoing due diligence under Rule 9(12) is not limited to account-opening and annual reviews, is not applied uniformly without regard to risk, and is distinct from the separate STR-filing obligation under the PML Rules. Note: Periodic updating of identification data and other client information appears in broader SEBI CDD guidance rather than within the Rule 9(12) text itself; entities should refer to the specific provision they are relying on.
